statusDefinitions.enforced: Every named control for the narrowly described current surface has implementation and automated verification evidence.

statusDefinitions.planned: The surface is not supported and must remain disabled until its acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
statusDefinitions.release-blocked: The current controls are insufficient for production qualification of the named surface; the recorded gate must remain pending.

risks.title: Malformed or oversized project documents
risks.actor: A user or collaborator supplies a corrupt or adversarial project document.

currentControls.summary: Core project migration validates retained schemas and opens newer schemas as opaque clones read-only without overwriting them. Schema 9 normalizes a bounded declarative feature-requirements manifest into a deep-frozen clone, rejecting duplicate requirement IDs, noncanonical feature IDs, unsupported dispositions, and invalid fallback source-kind references or digest syntax. Its pure evaluator classifies caller-declared availability without executing project-supplied identifiers or mutating the manifest. Current-schema, current-format .scape paths preserve the manifest and fallback-only source assets, including collision remapping. On current-format exact schema 9 routes, each rendered-fallback claim is bound to its canonical asset descriptor before collision lookup or storage. Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records, serializes those same sources and the bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation, rejects project/source toJSON rewrites, and hashes completed asset output before manifest write or destination commit; import verifies each asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding but does not hash asset bodies. A stable selected-product capability registry treats only strict `true` as available and unregistered IDs as unknown. Current schema 9 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the reserved `soundscaper.audio-effects` requirement for maintained first-party effects in track, group, send, or master racks, including disabled effects and inactive racks; publisher-authored audio-effects requirements take precedence, missing and foreign effects do not trigger it, and reserved-ID conflicts reject. The same paths reconcile the reserved `soundscaper.video-effects` requirement for maintained first-party effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips, including disabled effects; publisher-authored video-effects requirements take precedence, missing and foreign effects and stacks on non-video clips do not trigger it, and reserved-ID conflicts reject. Exact schema 9 is evaluated from the actual project history before activation, incompatible projects become intrinsically read-only, and an existing same-ID tab's stored read-only declaration wins over the ignored incoming document's flags. The report remains deep-frozen across per-tab session metadata clones and the document snapshot. Current-format .scape inspection receives the same selected-product evaluator as a provider-owned option that caller options cannot override; exact schema 9 is evaluated after archive and source validation but before project collision lookup and returns a deep-frozen report, while future schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. Maintained workspace/UI file-open routes turn incompatible exact-schema reports into one closed decision: no-collision permits only open-read-only or cancel, and a combined incompatibility and collision permits only copy-read-only or cancel. Cancel settles before native import, persistence, or activation. Acceptance passes only copy into native open, after which the controller reevaluates the actual project history and enforces it as intrinsically read-only. The localized dialog shows bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition, defaults focus to Cancel, and supports Escape dismissal and focus restoration. After activation, the maintained active workspace persistently displays a non-dismissible document-level notice from the active tab's incompatible report. It derives a frozen subset containing only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes counts, and shows bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared dispositions while the owning tab is active. Available items are excluded, evaluator messages and fallback internals are not read, and the notice exposes no activation controls or generic runtime fallback or third-party-loading claim; the separate exact first-party audio playback control binds its active indicator to frozen metadata. Compatible and future-schema null reports render no notice. For an exact schema 9 registered `audioEffects` item that is unavailable with declared `bypass` and effective `bypassed`, activation derives a bounded, non-persisted engine projection before activation side effects while the canonical project, history, source loading, and persistence remain unchanged. Only active, enabled, not already bypassed maintained first-party effects in track, group, send, and master racks become minimal bypassed playback copies. The lower-only 4,096-effect ceiling rejects instead of truncating; effect params, context, and state are not read. Deep-frozen per-tab and snapshot metadata drives one affected-object inventory with localized labels and no controls under the first qualifying requirement. Unknown and third-party effects, rendered fallback, offline render and export behavior, and activation controls remain outside this audio slice. For an exact schema 9 registered `videoEffects` item that is unavailable with declared `bypass` and effective `bypassed`, activation derives a bounded, non-persisted preview-playback projection before activation side effects while the canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save paths, offline render, and video export remain unchanged. Enabled maintained first-party effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips become minimal disabled engine copies. The lower-only 4,096-effect ceiling, 256-character stable-ID ceiling, and 128-character effect-type ceiling reject instead of truncating; effect params, context, state, and opaque payloads are not read. A per-snapshot cached selector removes only exact timeline clip-ID, effect-ID, and effect-type matches before compositor rendering and active-effect counting while preserving unchanged stack references; Project Bin inventory is not a compositor input. Each placeholder entry in the deep-frozen per-tab and snapshot metadata records only Timeline or Project Bin location, clip ID, effect ID, and effect type and drives one affected-object inventory with localized labels, canonical clip ownership, and no controls under the first qualifying requirement. Future schemas return before clip or Project Bin traversal. Already-disabled, foreign, unknown, and third-party effects, rendered fallback, offline render and export behavior, activation controls, and earlier Soundscaper project schemas remain outside this video slice. A separate maintained-controller admission control verifies exact-schema-9 raw and stored-project fallback bytes; arbitrary direct store loads remain outside that admission control. A separate first-party audio rendered-fallback playback control implements the exact-schema-9 whole-mix exception. Generic runtime fallback substitution beyond that narrow slice, generic unavailable-feature placeholders beyond the maintained first-party audio and video inventories, general per-feature activation controls, and arbitrary future-schema preservation remain outside this control. Complete third-party activation gating is a separate later surface rather than a prerequisite for these first-party notices.

Maintained controller admission verifies every rendered fallback in the authoritative exact-schema-9 activation project, including existing same-ID tab history bound by a session-owned history token, against referenced local bytes before activation side effects. After verification the controller obtains one exclusive session activation reservation before the first side effect; it rejects target history replacement, close/reopen, and competing active-project publication through synchronous session publication and is released in finally. Admission reads disable on-access PCM migration scheduling and retained-media digest claim/backfill, so verification does not publish storage maintenance. Audio hashes the canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence under checked PCM geometry and a cumulative 65,536-chunk ceiling; video hashes the genuine immutable original-media Blob body through the non-raiseable 4 MiB digest window. Unique claimed audio bytes and admitted video sizes share a non-raiseable 64 GiB cumulative ceiling before fallback body reads. Verification is sequential and cooperatively cancellable through the maintained store. Read-only video-metadata preflight is raced against cancellation, so an injected signal-ignoring provider may continue after admission rejects; a provider-stalled fallback body read can instead delay cancellation settlement and iterator cleanup. Verification deduplicates matching claims, rejects conflicting digests before storage reads, rejects missing or mismatched assets, and performs no asset read or featureRequirements traversal for future schemas. This is point-in-time controller admission: it does not verify arbitrary direct store.loadProject calls, continuously bind against later low-level source replacement, establish publisher authenticity, substitute fallback media at runtime, preserve arbitrary future schemas, provide affected-object placeholders or per-feature bypass controls, or complete third-party activation gating.

For exact schema 9, one registered audioEffects item that is unavailable with declared and effective rendered-fallback dispositions activates only when its descriptor exactly matches the canonical manifest. The referenced source must be mono or stereo, use its full safe frame range as one whole-mix clip from frame zero, and match project sample rate and master channel count; ADM, surround, ambiguous candidates, descriptor drift, unsafe geometry, missing media, and reserved synthetic ID collisions reject. The transient projection removes canonical audio clips and tracks, installs neutral playback state, neutralizes mixer and master processing, and retains video and label timing. Initial activation and later engine reapplies share the same playback service. Required stored metadata is rechecked; short sources are decoded and their buffer geometry must match exactly, while oversized sources must expose a streamable chunk provider. Readiness does not prefetch or revalidate streamed chunks, so later provider failure remains possible. A readiness failure prevents the projected engine load. Canonical project, history, persistence, save, export, and offline render stay unchanged, while deeply frozen tab and snapshot metadata drives a localized active during editor playback indicator without exposing source identity or digest. Controller digest admission is point-in-time, not a durable byte lease. The canonical identity fence suppresses stale engine apply, but stale source preparation can publish cache or provider state; activation source failure occurs after tab, lock, and session publication and does not roll those side effects back. Generic or video fallback, ADM or surround playback, freeze or proxy authoring, unknown or third-party activation, future schemas, and earlier Soundscaper schemas remain outside this control.
AUP4 conversion sanitizes imported records and is exercised with corrupt and compatibility fixtures.

A format-specific legacy `.aup` XML structural budget caps authoritative declared `File.size` and independently measures the returned text's UTF-8 byte length at 16 MiB, with at most 100,000 retained elements, 400,000 attributes, and maximum depth at 128 through lower-only test seams. Limits reject before any legacy `_data` block read, conversion, project/source persistence, or imported-project publication. This narrow control does not qualify elapsed time, other project families, selected `_data` bytes or decoded PCM amplification, or the total import working set.

Supported canonical, default-sized legacy `.aup` simple and silent block materialization has non-raiseable production ceilings and lower-only test seams: 65,536 selected companion files and 65,536 materializing references, 2 MiB per referenced physical file, 1 MiB per AU sample payload, 524,288 decoded or silent frames per block, 512 MiB of authoritative unique referenced `File.size`, and 512 MiB of retained Float32 PCM including repeated references, silence, and linked-track zero-fill. Bounded exact/basename indexes prevent reference-by-file lookup multiplication; positive block lengths, the 24-byte AU header minimum, and equal-length paired linked clips are required. Checked admission covers selected/reference counts, declared bytes, and retained PCM before retained-PCM allocation or block reads, while AU payload/frame checks precede decoded-block allocation. Actual `ArrayBuffer.byteLength` must equal snapshotted declared size. Audacity's native-endian AU representation is accepted, each unique file is read and decoded once, and one preallocated output per physical clip makes the logically reachable parser-owned pending window beyond retained PCM at most one 2 MiB encoded file plus one 2 MiB decoded block. Equal or admitted zero-padded linked channels pass conversion without channel-normalization copies. Refusal precedes conversion, project/source persistence, and imported-project publication. This format-specific control does not qualify XML-tree or opaque-extension clone amplification, elapsed time or cancellation, aliases, customized Audacity block-size settings above the policy ceilings, provider-internal copies or garbage-collection lag, downstream conversion/waveform/storage/persistence working sets, total renderer RSS, noncanonical AU padding, other project families, or streaming-scale legacy import.

residualRisks.exposure: Legacy `.aup` XML and supported canonical, default-sized simple/silent `_data` materialization have format-specific structural, referenced-input, block-geometry, retained-PCM, indexed-lookup, and parser-owned pending-window budgets. The shared-project codec now applies a raw-JSON structural preflight to every schema before `JSON.parse` under a non-raiseable ceiling of 101,536 JSON values and depth 130, including the worst-case tagged-binary wire expansion; exact schema 9 is then decoded and structurally admitted by the semantic validator under independent ceilings of 100,000 logical nodes and depth 128. The main service exposes lower-only seams for those limits across renderer input, loaded commit results, stored reads, and response serialization. Over-budget renderer input refuses before host commit or staging; an over-budget loaded commit result refuses before the renderer response but may follow host publication. The lexical preflight, decoded-codec traversal, validation admission, and response serialization reset their counters and remain per-phase shape bounds rather than one aggregate execution budget. CPU or elapsed time, cancellation, scalar and string work, IPC and JSON/string allocation, semantic normalization and clone amplification, provider-internal allocation, garbage-collection lag, and total main-process RSS remain unqualified. The hostile-input claim covers canonical JSON-derived production graphs and ordinary direct objects, not arbitrary in-realm proxies or malicious injected hosts or providers. Other supported project parsers still do not share aggregate byte, node, depth, or elapsed-time budgets, while XML-tree and opaque-extension cloning, aliases, customized Audacity block sizes above policy ceilings, downstream conversion/waveform/storage/persistence amplification, total renderer RSS, cancellation, and streaming-scale legacy import remain outside this qualification.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Apply documented structural budgets to the remaining project families and qualify aggregate CPU or elapsed-time, cancellation, scalar-byte work, and end-to-end working-set budgets across repeated main shared-project phases and downstream legacy-import work.
acceptanceCriteria: Remaining project-family boundary tests reject oversized, over-node, and deeply nested fixtures before writes or renderer responses, while qualified aggregate cancellation, CPU or elapsed-time, scalar-byte, and end-to-end working-set budgets cover repeated main shared-project parser and validator phases plus downstream materialization.

residualRisks.exposure: Focused legacy `.aup` XML and AU-block boundary/no-publication fixtures cover declared and returned XML bytes, elements, attributes, depth, selected and referenced counts, indexed lookup and ambiguity, declared/actual block bytes and the header minimum, positive block and payload/frame geometry, native endianness, pre-allocation refusal, retained PCM, silence, repeated references, stereo padding, and unequal linked-pair rejection, but the maintained malformed-project corpus does not yet cover every supported project family.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Maintain regression and fuzz fixtures for each supported project parser.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs parser corpus tests with storage publication assertions for each family.

risks.title: Malformed media and metadata consume excessive resources or escape validation
risks.actor: An imported audio, video, metadata, or codec-argument payload is corrupt or adversarial.

currentControls.summary: WAV chunk iteration, metadata sizes, channel counts, and compressed ADM XML expansion have explicit bounds. Current BW64 import retains a complete ordered nonstructural RIFF chunk sequence only while aggregate complete chunk bytes, including headers and alignment bytes, stay at or below 16 MiB; incomplete capture is recorded and cannot promote to pristine passthrough.
Custom FFmpeg exports use allowlisted protocols and reject extra inputs, reports, and unbounded arguments.

residualRisks.exposure: Compressed audio and video decoders lack a broad maintained malformed-input corpus and resource-budget gate.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Add codec-family corpus tests and explicit decode memory, output, and elapsed-time budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: CI exercises truncated, oversized, recursive, and decompression-amplification fixtures without publishing partial output.

residualRisks.exposure: Future native decoding is not yet isolated from the UI process or covered by crash quarantine.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Run native decoders in a supervised helper with bounded IPC and documented OS sandbox policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Helper crash, timeout, oversized output, and malformed-message tests leave the editor process responsive.

risks.title: Portable project archive paths and descriptors reference unintended or altered content
risks.actor: A .scape archive contains unsafe names, duplicates, inconsistent descriptors, or altered payload bytes.

currentControls.summary: Import rejects absolute, backslash, traversal, and duplicate names, validates manifest descriptors, and verifies extracted size and SHA-256 before publishing the project. zip.js runs with `checkSignature: true` so extraction also enforces each entry CRC; a negative rollback regression corrupts stored-asset CRC metadata, observes signature rejection, and leaves target inventory unchanged.

Import and inspection share a strict metadata envelope that rejects encrypted and directory entries, duplicate source or entry ownership, reserved-entry reuse, descriptor aliases, missing entries, and unreferenced extra entries before project or source storage writes.

After project migration, import and inspection require equal source/descriptor counts, unique exact case-sensitive source IDs, and identical audio/video kinds before collision handling, transaction creation, or any storage call.

For current-format exact schema 9 archives, every rendered-fallback claim is bound to its canonical asset descriptor before compatibility evaluation, collision lookup, or storage. Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records, serializes those same sources and the bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation, rejects project-root/source-record accessors and callable toJSON hooks without invocation, and compares each completed, actually hashed asset digest before manifest write or destination commit. Import verifies the extracted asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding only and does not hash asset bodies; future-schema feature requirements remain opaque.

Every project schema receives a structural scan before `JSON.parse` under lower-only raw ceilings of 101,536 JSON values and depth 130. Those maxima include exact-schema-9's worst-case wire expansion for 256 tagged-binary payloads: six additional JSON values per payload and two additional depth levels preserve round-trip closure for lowered logical limits. Exact-schema-9, current-format export copies Uint8Array, offset-view, and ArrayBuffer bytes into a reserved versioned tag under independent lower-only ceilings of 256 payloads, 4 MiB per payload, 8 MiB aggregate bytes, 100,000 logical traversed nodes, and depth 128. Import and inspection validate closed descriptors, unique positive IDs, canonical base64, exact lengths, reserved-tag collisions, and the complete decoded budget before decoded-byte allocation, collision lookup, transaction creation, or storage. Decoding restores only the declared binary type and never interprets or activates its bytes. Project-container accessors, callable container toJSON hooks, cycles, unsupported binary views, malformed tags, and ambiguous tags reject. Other project schemas retain ordinary JSON values; tag-shaped future state is structurally scanned and counted but is not decoded or interpreted.

risks.title: Portable project archive expansion exhausts memory, storage, or execution time
risks.actor: A .scape archive uses large metadata, misleading sizes, compression amplification, or a malicious PCM header.

currentControls.summary: Import caps entry count, validates hashes after extraction, aborts a failing audio writer, deletes already staged sources, and saves the project last.
A strict TypeScript envelope validates the entry-count limit and safe integer compressed/uncompressed metadata for every file before reading manifest bytes.
Manifest JSON is capped at 32 MiB and project JSON at 256 MiB using both central-directory preflight and byte-counted streaming text sinks.
The envelope rejects central-directory declarations whose safe cumulative uncompressed size exceeds 64 GiB before reading any entry body.

One shared budget counts bytes actually emitted into the manifest, project, and every extracted asset sink, rejecting cumulative output above 64 GiB before the over-budget chunk is retained or published.

After validated manifest assets and the existing-project collision-cancel decision, but before copy remapping, transaction construction or capture, source metadata reads, writer creation, or asset extraction, import computes a checked safe-integer sum of every incoming asset size plus exact ceil(10%) headroom and obtains exactly one storage estimate. An existing-ID cancel performs no estimate; copy and replace each charge the full incoming asset total without credit for replaced content. An absent or unknown estimate permits import, while known insufficient free bytes throw stable frozen `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` details. The maintained native-controller route exclusively supplies a decorated preflight callback with the raw asset-byte total and captures the composed import task signal. Its storage-capacity service derives the same exact headroom requirement, publishes `checking` followed by `ready`, `unknown`, or `insufficient` in the workspace `lastPreflight` snapshot, and returns the one normalized estimate that drives the Scape quota decision. Cancellation promptly abandons a signal-ignoring estimate, closes the archive reader, starts no writer or extraction, restores the prior settled preflight snapshot, consumes late provider resolution or rejection, and generation-fences older work from replacing newer state. Standalone undecorated imports retain the optional direct store estimator and do not update controller state. The authentic 8 GiB sparse witness pins 8,589,932,094 asset bytes, exactly 9,448,925,304 required free bytes, and capacity estimation before its media writer. This is point-in-time admission only: it does not reserve capacity, establish real browser or filesystem quota accuracy, qualify durable OPFS or IndexedDB 8 GiB persistence, account for browser-record or filesystem-allocation overhead beyond the policy headroom, guarantee write-time success, or serialize concurrent writers.

Audio extraction validates each four-byte frame header against the shared 65,536-frame and 64-channel geometry limits before checked byte-length calculation or allocation; parser-owned pending storage is capped at 16 MiB plus the header.

Before manifest extraction, every entry runs zip.js strict local-header validation and pairwise entry-range overlap detection without decompressing its body; tested method disagreements and nested entry ranges reject before storage work.

A bounded raw-layout preflight, under a shared non-raiseable 33 MiB central-directory cap, anchors exact classic/Zip64 end and central-directory records, validates every central/local header and data descriptor without extracting or hashing entry bodies, and rejects gaps, overlap, or entry ranges crossing the central directory before zip.js construction. Its fixed ZIP end-record search can overlap at most 65,557 bytes of a final payload tail. Export admission reserves the pinned writer's greater-than-4-GiB Zip64 offset branch so produced archives remain admissible.

Archive validation and zip.js share a branded random-access byte source: providers declare a lower-only maximum beneath the non-raiseable 33 MiB logical read ceiling, and returned ranges are measured and copied through captured native `Uint8Array` slots. One exact 69,271,649-byte canonical-profile witness retains admitted end records, central headers, names, extras, comments, local structures, and descriptors; it rejects conflicting overlaps, serves witnessed bytes unchanged, and fetches only payload gaps. Blob behavior remains covered by parity tests. A zero-high-water-mark ZIP payload stream makes overlap-only checks lazy instead of prefetching the start of a large entry. Main assigns terminal canonical `.scape` projects the immutable `scape-range-v1` profile, while Audacity and other desktop inputs remain `materialized-v1`. The strict renderer adapter snapshots the descriptor URL/declared size and fetch implementation, splits reads into exact at-most-16-MiB `206` responses, serializes through stream done, and terminally fences the first admitted abort or transport failure without exposing release authority. Project-dialog and OS-association `.scape` descriptors share one explicit router and awaited scope spanning inspection, any open decision, import, and exact-once release. The inspection collision-cancel witness traverses structural inspection and collision lookup before cancellation, transfers less than 8 MiB, touches the huge body only through the at-most-65,557-byte suffix overlapped by the ZIP end-record search, and does not hash that body. Its authentic exact 8 GiB sparse Zip64 current-schema fixture binds the 8,589,932,094-byte all-zero asset to SHA-256 7feeb1e9eacb6561f3c5afb4ebf3896c8237660a9b4ed8917d3275c79bed38be and CRC-32 2,909,126,900. A separate witness takes the full payload through the real read-capability store, Node protocol shim, renderer adapter, file service, project service, and full import into an independent counting-SHA-256 transactional sink with zero payload retention and no Blob materialization; its point-in-time import-capacity estimate precedes the media writer and admits the exact 9,448,925,304-byte free-space requirement, capability release occurs exactly once, and the pinned handle close occurs exactly once. That full-import witness remains verified reference evidence and is exposed as the opt-in portable reference-scale gate `npm run test:reference:scape-8gib`. Routine Node and coverage runs fast-skip it because a measured all-files coverage run passed but took 525 seconds. This scheduling does not demote or narrow the verified result; collision-cancel inspection and the corrupted-CRC negative rollback remain in routine coverage. Both witnesses require sparse-file support and use a Node protocol shim, not packaged UI. The counting sink does not qualify OPFS or IndexedDB durable 8 GiB persistence, real browser or filesystem quota accuracy or reservation, write-time success under concurrent writers, browser heap or process RSS, whole-storage atomicity, or publisher authentication.

Archive enumeration is hard-capped at 4,096 entries, bounding zip.js pairwise layout comparisons, and one archive-wide budget is capped at 65,536 canonical PCM chunks before another source-writer call or chunk allocation.
Every project or asset descriptor must exactly match its entry's declared uncompressed size before project JSON or asset extraction begins.
The manifest, project, and asset descriptors must own distinct expected entries, and all extra, alias, missing, directory, or reserved-name entries are rejected before storage work.
Any encrypted central-directory entry rejects the archive before manifest or project bytes are read.
Inspection and import call the same strict archive-envelope validator; an integration test proves both reject the same extra entry before storage writes.
Central-directory indexing requires ZIP STORE and equal compressed/uncompressed sizes before local-header preflight or body reads; canonical exports pin the same policy.

Original video entries emit at most 4 MiB per zip.js chunk, are charged and independently hashed before each awaited transactional storage write, and must match declared size and SHA-256 before publication. OPFS receives bounded writes; IndexedDB uses source-owned native Blob chunks; process-memory fallback rejects payloads above 64 MiB before extraction. Cancellation, metadata drift, and failed publication remove staging and preserve prior inventory.

Canonical save output is re-chunked to at most 4 MiB, constrained by the admitted archive maximum, and verified by independent byte counts before publication. File System Access and desktop project targets remain staged until an explicit commit; desktop additionally negotiates one-MiB acknowledged IPC writes and synced rename. The non-streaming browser-download fallback retains its non-raiseable 512 MiB final-Blob ceiling.

The tested .scape open/save path propagates one task AbortSignal through ZIP enumeration and extraction, source reads and writes, archive output, and file publication. Cancellation closes readers, returns source iterators, aborts unpublished destinations and audio writers, deletes provisional media, and restores the prior project plus its retained revisions.

risks.title: Current Electron renderer IPC reaches privileges outside the versioned bridge
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content attempts to invoke arbitrary Electron or Node.js capabilities.

currentControls.summary: The renderer has context isolation, no Node integration, a sandbox, and a frozen input-validating v1 bridge. Its shared-project methods are bounded, pathless list, read, commit, and delete operations whose return values are independently sanitized in main.

Main-process handlers require the expected webContents and root document URL while navigation, new windows, webviews, and unapproved permissions are denied. Shared-project owner revocation fences new operations and drains operations admitted before navigation, renderer loss, or window close.

risks.title: Current desktop static-resource requests escape the packaged application root
risks.actor: Renderer content crafts an encoded path, symlink path, method, or range request.

currentControls.summary: Static requests are decoded, canonicalized, constrained by realpath containment, limited to safe methods, and protected by the desktop CSP.

risks.title: Desktop read capabilities leak paths, outlive their owner, or allow unbounded working sets
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses or accumulates capabilities, or triggers a large whole-file read.

currentControls.summary: User selection opens a regular file first, returns a high-entropy expiring token rather than a path, and serves bounded single ranges from the pinned handle.

The immutable main-assigned read profile is bound through the store entry, frozen descriptor, canonical URL, lookup, and request lease. Unknown or mismatched profiles and malformed range requests refuse before lease acquisition or TTL renewal, and the store repeats expected-profile comparison before renewal. `scape-range-v1` accepts only `GET` with one exact closed range wholly inside the declared file, caps it at 16 MiB, and always responds `206`; full-file, `HEAD`, suffix, open-ended, multiple, oversized, and EOF-overrun requests refuse. One shared Scape admission gate permits one active range request globally. A successful Web response body must reach done before its lease releases, preserving the pinned handle for a later request. Body cancellation, request abort, or inner stream failure fences and retires the entire capability, waits for native stream close and pinned handle close, and settles the renderer after that cleanup barrier; explicit release, expiry, owner revocation, and shutdown join the same retirement. A failed cleanup tombstone remains visible only to the correct owner until owner or store teardown, token allocation cannot alias it, and lookup exposes no raw handle. Preload validation repeats exact profile, name, MIME, profile-size, and canonical URL-path rules with no query or fragment. Renderer validation excludes Scape from generic materialization, admits only canonical `scape-range-v1` descriptors to the strict archive adapter, verifies each partial response through stream done, and owns exact release after success, failure, cancellation, abort, or invalid routing. Project-dialog and OS-association `.scape` descriptors share that awaited scope; browser Blob and materialized Audacity or other paths are unchanged.

Every pending or published desktop read capability is bound to the opaque main-owned identity of the currently committed main-frame document. Main selects one immutable profile and both profiles share at most 128 pending or live capability slots per owner, reserved before the first file-open await. `materialized-v1` retains a non-raiseable 512 MiB aggregate declared-byte ceiling per owner. Canonical terminal Scape projects use the independent `scape-range-v1` admission of at most four capabilities and 65 GiB aggregate declared bytes both globally and per owner; count reserves before open and bytes charge after stat but before publication. A failed candidate or retirement cleanup retains its range charge and fences new range admission. Wrong-owner release refuses without revealing, removing, or closing the capability. Correct release and expiry synchronously remove it from lookup before draining its handle. Navigation, renderer loss, window close, and shutdown fence the affected owner or store before draining every admitted open and handle close; delayed dialog, open, or stat completion closes without publication. Partial multi-file registration drains every rollback release and reports primary plus cleanup failures. OS-open paths remain serially deduplicated at one visible queue head. With four real Scape descriptors admitted globally, the fifth refuses before open and remains queued; one acknowledged release redispatches it. A renderer-send failure releases its descriptor before reporting and removing that head. Transient count or aggregate-byte pressure is retryable without eviction, but an individually oversized file is not. Revocation and shutdown attempt every close before rejecting on cleanup failure, and shutdown permanently refuses new admission.

This control applies only to main-assigned `materialized-v1` descriptors. Authoritative main-process admission limits their aggregate active declared selected-file bytes to a non-raiseable 512 MiB per committed-document owner before publication. The preload validates the exact materialized profile, name, MIME, safe size, and canonical profile-bearing URL. The renderer repeats profile admission before fetch and rejects any Scape name, canonical Scape MIME, or `scape-range-v1` descriptor instead of materializing it. For admitted materialized reads it requires exact declared Content-Length, emitted-byte, and final Blob-size agreement and reads only the response body stream. Retained parts are copied and split at the non-raiseable 16 MiB platform media-chunk limit. The materializer forwards the caller's AbortSignal, promptly races and cancels a stalled body read with its exact reason, and never calls response.blob(). A scoped descriptor batch releases every capability after its callback on success, failure, or cancellation, while request abort destroys the protocol file stream. This is a bounded whole-Blob tier, not a bound on decoder amplification or whole-process RSS; Scape is excluded and handled by the separately admitted range profile.

risks.title: Desktop saves overwrite unintended paths, leave partial files, or exhaust disk
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses a target or sends inconsistent, oversized, or interrupted chunks.

currentControls.summary: A user-selected target becomes a short-lived single-use token; sequential one-MiB chunks are checked against an exact length and committed by synced same-directory rename with abort cleanup.

Only project save capabilities may select bounded streaming mode. Main rejects writes above the archive-admitted maximum, waits for an active chunk acknowledgement before abort cleanup, and removes sessions on navigation, renderer loss, window close, or shutdown; explicit finish remains the sync-and-rename commit boundary.

A dedicated `audio-pcm-mix` purpose permits only WAV, AIFF, BWF, and BW64 target names without granting generic audio targets maximum-bounded streaming authority. The maintained direct PCM route admits one mix only when its plan has one output and `realtime-stream`. WAV requires `audio/wav`, `.wav`, and one positive safe-integer planned file byte count at or below 65 GiB; AIFF requires `audio/aiff`, `.aiff`, and an exact count at or below 4,294,967,303 bytes, its theoretical 32-bit FORM limit. Direct admission requires an explicit valid sample rate, 1–32 channels, from zero through 4,294,967,295 output frames, non-array object metadata, and one canonical (`sampleFormat`, `bitDepth`, `floatingPoint`) tuple: (`int16`, 16, false), (`int24`, 24, false), (`int32`, 32, false), or (`float32`, 32, true). It recomputes `inspectAiffLayout` from those same layout-affecting encoder options, requires AIFF for integer PCM or AIFF-C for float32, and requires its exact byte count to equal the plan. Malformed or stale fields and layouts reject before target selection. The 4,294,967,303-byte theoretical maximum is odd and unconstructible under the current aligned layout; a layout-only witness allocates no PCM or output bytes while admitting the largest current constructible 4,294,967,302-byte layout and rejecting its next mono int16 frame. Exact integer AIFF, AIFF-C float, odd PCM padding, and trailing ID3 metadata use that same encoder geometry. BWF requires `audio/wav`, `.wav`, and one positive safe-integer planned file byte count at or below 65 GiB. Admission requires an explicit valid sample rate, 1–32 channels, a nonnegative safe-integer frame count, object metadata, a marker array, and null-or-object iXML and CART. It recomputes the automatic RIFF/RF64 layout with `inspectWavLayout` from the same encoder options used by streaming: sample rate, channel count, frame count, integer precision, BEXT, metadata, markers, iXML, and CART. It rejects malformed fields or a planned-byte mismatch before target selection. Its plan and encoding must carry the same canonical normalized version-2 BEXT, and only integer int16, int20, or int24 PCM is admitted. It rejects a plan container, ADM, `preDataChunks`, and `trailingChunks`, keeping BW64 and opaque chunks outside the direct BWF variant; rich standard BWF metadata, markers, iXML, and CART remain eligible when their exact geometry agrees. A layout-only witness allocates no PCM or output bytes while admitting the exact constructible 69,793,218,560-byte (65 GiB) RF64 boundary and rejecting the next frame. This remains an admission ceiling, not BWF scale, package, heap, or RSS qualification. Authored BW64 requires format and container `bw64`, `audio/wav`, `.wav`, and an exact positive safe-integer layout recomputed by `inspectWavLayout` at or below 69,793,218,560 bytes (65 GiB). This is a 65 GiB admission ceiling, not an exercised scale claim. Only int16, int20, or int24 PCM with the same canonical normalized version-2 BEXT in the plan and encoding is admitted. ADM must be authored normalized ADM for mono, stereo, or 5.1, with exact bed channel order and an identity preserve mapping. Canonical CHNA before PCM and AXML after PCM must be byte-identical in `plan.adm` and the top-level plan. Standard RIFF metadata, markers, iXML, and CART remain inside exact geometry. The separately admitted pristine-passthrough BW64 route is qualified only for metadata produced by the current BW64 importer and still accepted by the pristine planner: valid warning-free ADM, one unchanged neutral full-range source path at the import revision, and a nonempty complete `riffChunkSequence` whose aggregate complete nonstructural RIFF bytes, including headers and alignment bytes, do not exceed 16 MiB. Direct admission rechecks 1–32 channels of int16, int20, or int24 non-float PCM; exact rate, channel, frame, and precision geometry; zero tail and dither; full range; identity preserve mappings in plan and encoding; CHNA-derived channel order; exact compacted pre/post bytes, order, and placement in `plan.adm` and the top-level plan; and exact `inspectWavLayout` geometry under the same 65 GiB admission ceiling. A preserved BEXT is emitted only from the sequence; without one, plan and encoding must carry the same canonical normalized version-2 BEXT. Preserved cue/adtl, iXML, CART, ID3, or LIST/INFO chunks suppress their modeled plan fields, and collisions reject. Legacy `opaqueRiffChunks`-only metadata, incomplete capture, invalid or warning-bearing metadata, stale or edited projects, sequence drift, mapping or geometry drift, and loudness measurement reject before target selection. The byte-exact claim covers preserved nonstructural chunks only; structural BW64 and PCM bytes are rebuilt, so this is not whole-file bit identity or broad third-party BW64 qualification. A direct-eligible realtime BWF or BW64 request with `measureLoudness: true` fails closed before target, preflight, or render because bounded two-pass measurement is unimplemented; there is no measured-loudness claim. Desktop save-choice policy permits `.wav`, `.aif`, and `.aiff`, while direct controller admission remains canonical `.wav` or `.aiff`. An exact-size, not maximum-bounded File System Access or Electron session receives the planned count; desktop receives `size` rather than `maximumSize` and rejects an underwrite before publication. The shared PCM adapter is fed by 16,384-frame chunks with a channel-aware pending count that bounds queued planar Float32 PCM to 32 MiB, propagates realtime progress into the owned task UI, and resamples a selection-only upmix before duplicating its selected channels. It has bounded encoder-emission retention, coalesces PCM into at-most-4-MiB destination writes, and serially awaits each write. Exact desktop `audio-pcm-mix` sessions negotiate four-MiB chunks while generic exact-size and project sessions remain at one MiB. Planned, encoder-finalized, destination-written, and committed-result byte counts must form a four-way agreement, and explicit commit occurs with no final renderer `Blob`. BW64 passthrough outside the exact current-import contract, including legacy opaque-only metadata, plus other PCM containers, compressed or custom audio, video, stems, non-realtime plans, and browser-download Blob fallback remain outside this route. Focused Node AIFF evidence has four cases covering exact FORM and metadata geometry, closed admission across all four canonical encoding tuples, malformed and stale layout refusal before target selection, the exact 4,294,967,302-byte constructible boundary and next-frame refusal without PCM or output allocation, realtime direct publication, picker cancellation, and mid-stream rollback. Focused Node BWF evidence has five cases covering admission, exact layout and publication, loudness fail-closed behavior, four-way diagnostics, and mid-stream cancellation. Focused Node authored BW64 evidence has six cases covering closed admission, exact standard-metadata preparation, canonical ds64/BEXT/fmt/CHNA/data/AXML streaming, loudness fail-closed behavior, four-way diagnostics, and mid-stream cancellation. Seven focused pristine-passthrough BW64 cases cover the real current-import-to-planner route, preserved and generated BEXT branches, exact nonstructural chunk bytes/order/placement and publication, closed admission, modeled-metadata collision refusal, stale or edited planning refusal, and loudness fail-closed behavior; the full maintained Node suite is green at 383 test files. Focused WAV tests retain completion, cancellation, shared write bounds, and cleanup. An opt-in Node desktop-threshold witness streams an exact 385 MiB silent float payload into a 403,701,804-byte RIFF with pinned SHA-256 through the production planner, controller, real 16-packet queue at its 32-channel, 32 MiB cap, passthrough resampler, WAV encoder, and counting target. It requests 193 16,384-frame packets with a half-sized final packet, observes at most 16 pending packets, and makes 98 destination writes including the header with a 4,194,304-byte maximum. Its conservative 41,943,384-byte path-owned binary maximum is below the planned 64 MiB buffered-binary budget with zero PCM payload retention; a second run cancels after the first coalesced 4 MiB PCM destination write without close, commit, or partial publication. Maintained Chromium and Firefox WAV, AIFF, BWF, and BW64 coverage comprises ten aggregate format/engine cases through an injected File System Access target and simulated mobile planner profile. The BWF case retains a 2 KiB prefix and validates RIFF, bext, fmt, and data geometry, an authored description, a 64-bit TimeReference, and two-row CodingHistory. The authored BW64 case uses a 33.1-second stereo source and 384 kHz 16-bit output; its 101,683,200-byte float-plan geometry exceeds 96 MiB but is not a final-file or scale qualification. A bounded 2 KiB prefix and 8 KiB suffix validate BW64, ds64, BEXT, fmt, canonical stereo CHNA, data, and trailing AXML. The pristine-passthrough case imports a synthetic 5.1, 48 kHz, 16-bit BW64 with 4,210,688 frames; its 101,056,512-byte float-plan geometry also exceeds 96 MiB without qualifying final-file scale. Bounded 2 KiB prefix and 4 KiB suffix retention proves exact source JUNK padding, BEXT v2, and CHNA bytes/order before PCM plus PEAK padding and AXML bytes/order after PCM. Visible realtime progress precedes completed close, commit, and publication without Object URL or browser-download fallback. A second export cancels after nonzero PCM reaches the target and observes one abort without close, commit, or publication. All destination writes are at most 4 MiB and serial. The authored BW64 case passed focused Chromium and Firefox runs in 42.2 and 45.8 seconds; the pristine-passthrough case passed in 1.7 and 1.8 minutes respectively. The six earlier cases were not freshly rerun together. This qualifies current-import application-path browser plumbing, selected preserved nonstructural chunk bytes/order/placement, publication, and pre-commit rollback, not arbitrary third-party or legacy opaque-only BW64, edited projects, whole-file bit identity, native-picker availability, the 65 GiB ceiling at scale, packaged behavior, heap or RSS, crash, power loss, or durability. WebKit remains unqualified because its pinned runtime cannot launch on this host. Packaged Soundscaper Linux x64 acceptance drives Electron 43 UI, controller, preload IPC, and `AtomicSaveManager`: a 48-kHz two-channel 792,000-frame encoded input was observed as a 791,999-frame project range and produced 6,335,992 signed-16-bit frames at 384 kHz and 16 channels. The 405,503,488-byte float plan exceeds 384 MiB and the final RIFF is 202,751,788 bytes. EOF and diagnostic SHA-256 verification uses at-most-one-MiB reads and at-most-31-byte carry, compares 95,039,880 channel samples with zero mismatches, and applies tolerant signal bounds. Cancellation independently observed a 33,554,476-byte staging file through an at-most-65,536-byte valid-RIFF prefix with nonzero payload, then verified destination and staging cleanup; no browser download appeared. CI is scoped to Soundscaper Linux x64. The smoke validates save choice then bypasses the native picker. The 385 MiB witness and packaged claims apply to WAV only, with no BWF or BW64 scale qualification. AIFF, BWF, and BW64 have no packaged, native-picker, heap, RSS, or platform qualification. The 65 GiB BW64 ceiling is admission only, not scale qualification. The WAV smoke does not qualify heap or RSS, quota, durability, crash or power loss, Windows, macOS, ARM, installers, Framescaper, or other formats. Exact frame geometry is Electron-runtime-specific and must be revisited on upgrade; the hash is not pinned and commit-race acceptance remains Node-only.

Shutdown synchronously rejects new target and save-session admission, drains operations admitted before the fence through any sync-and-rename commit, aborts remaining or late-opened staging, and exposes one idempotent disposal barrier that rejects on unacknowledged handle close or staging removal.

Every target and derived session is bound to one committed main-document owner. Owner revocation on main-document navigation, renderer loss, or actual window close synchronously fences admission, invalidates unconsumed targets including delayed dialog results, drains admitted begin, chunk, finish, and abort operations through any admitted sync-and-rename commit, then aborts remaining staging. Fresh-owner session admission waits for that drain so a stale commit cannot overtake a replacement save.

Main enforces 16 outstanding product-wide targets, 4 pending or live sessions, and 65 GiB per-save and aggregate admitted bytes, covering the canonical 64 GiB expanded `.scape` envelope plus its bounded STORE/ZIP overhead. Global count and byte reservations are taken synchronously before the first await, and production ceilings expose lower-only test seams. A fail-closed bigint `statfs` available-space check completes before staging open. The check is point-in-time admission, not an operating-system reservation; charges release only after no staging was acquired, an acknowledged cleanup, or a completed commit, and a staging cleanup failure leaves them charged.

residualRisks.exposure: A bounded IPC chunk must finish or fail before abort closes staging; sync/rename is the non-cancellable commit boundary, and parent-directory durability is not qualified.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define the cancellation acknowledgement and platform durability contract for active save operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Fault-injection tests cover cancellation during write, sync, and rename on every supported desktop platform.

risks.title: Shared desktop projects, their renderer bridge, or their catalog publish inconsistently across product ownership
risks.actor: A compromised renderer, competing or crashed desktop product, or malformed or tampered appData project document attempts invalid, stale, or inconsistent publication.

currentControls.summary: A fresh filesystem library scope v2 ignores rather than migrates the prior shared v1 scope; a schema 1 database found at the v2 path is rejected instead of implicitly migrated. Metadata schema 2 binds a separate opaque library entry ID to the project identity, exact schema 9, project revision, bounded byte length, SHA-256, and derived immutable revision-and-digest path. The main project store uses the canonical tagged-binary codec, enforces the non-raiseable 256 MiB document ceiling through a lower-only test seam, validates the persistence root identity, and reserves each canonical immutable path in a lease- and fencing-token-bound authoritative project-file inventory before stage creation. Before `JSON.parse` constructs an object graph, every schema receives a structural scan under raw ceilings of 101,536 JSON values and depth 130, including the worst-case tagged-binary descriptor expansion. Exact schema 9 then receives independent decoded-codec and semantic-validator ceilings of 100,000 logical nodes and depth 128 per phase. The main-owned editor service exposes lower-only seams for these limits across renderer input, loaded commit results, stored reads, and response serialization. An over-budget renderer input rejects before host commit or project staging. A loaded commit result may be rejected after the host has already published it, but neither that result nor an over-budget stored read reaches the renderer response. The lexical preflight, decoded-codec traversal, validator admission, and response serialization reset their counters and do not constitute one aggregate CPU, elapsed-time, cancellation, allocation, or RSS budget. Structural admission is qualified for canonical JSON-derived production graphs and ordinary direct objects, not arbitrary in-realm proxies or malicious injected hosts or providers. Within that scope, accessors, callable toJSON hooks, method-shadowed arrays, hidden or symbol data, cycles, exotic containers, and non-JSON scalars reject without invoking application accessors. The store writes a private file, syncs it, atomically renames it, syncs the containing directory where supported, marks the inventory row materialized, reverifies length, digest, schema, ID, and revision, and requires every catalog reference to have a materialized row before an exact plus-one catalog journal publication. The main-owned editor service runs the strict exact-schema-9 maintained-persistence-domain validator before calling host commit and therefore before project staging; it repeats validation on loaded commit results and stored reads before returning a renderer response. Core project, document, media, and graph structures are strictly checked. All audio effects must be cloneable and carry their generic identity, enabled, and parameter structure; type-specific semantic checks cover missing-effect compatibility metadata and parametric EQ, while other first- and third-party effect payload semantics are intentionally not gated. Adversarial fixtures reject invalid collection shapes, duplicate identities, dangling source or clip references, over-node and deeply nested shapes, non-enumerable or accessor-backed ordinary properties, array method shadows, non-JSON scalar values, and invalid loaded commit results. Input-side failures do not reach a host commit or project file, and the packaged runtime fixture proves both validation and structural admission are emitted and active. Lease ownership is checked before staging, before publication, and transactionally at catalog commit. The host serializes commits and renews its lease while close drains admitted work. The shared-project surface of the identity service, frozen preload, and owner-scoped IPC exposes only bounded pathless list, read, commit, and delete operations. Main and preload independently enforce the 256 MiB document, 4 KiB identity, and 10,000-summary ceilings; catalog summaries omit entry IDs, main-owned catalog/filesystem paths, digests, product preferences, raw `updatedAtMs` fields, leases, and fencing tokens. Renderer-owner revocation fences new work and drains admitted operations. The renderer repository repeats maintained-persistence-domain exact-schema-9 validation and canonical reserialization before local mutation, treats the shared latest document and summary list as authoritative, retains a product-local revision, source, and media shadow, and fails closed on an incomplete desktop bridge. A composed source-free editor fixture creates and autosaves in Soundscaper, discovers and bootstrap-reopens the same identity and revision from a fresh Framescaper-local store, publishes the next revision under a higher fencing token, and leaves the shared media catalog empty.

A maintained dedicated Linux x64 CI job builds two separate unpacked Soundscaper and Framescaper packages, then runs sequential Soundscaper to Framescaper to Soundscaper processes. The processes share only one isolated appData root, use separate product profiles, and the return stage reuses the Soundscaper profile. Each process waits for renderer ready, drives bounded pathless preload IPC, exact-SHA-256 verifies the expected canonical source-free schema 9 document, commits revisions 1, 2, and 3, checks the renderer summary and main-only catalog row, requires clean recovery, no stale takeover, higher fencing tokens, increasing catalog revisions, and the expected preferred product, and awaits process exit and lease release before the next stage. Combined with the composed editor fixture, this closes only the generic packaged source-free preload/IPC/multi-process/executable lifecycle gap. It does not qualify packaged controller autosave or tab activation; source-bearing bytes, playback, or managed media; concurrent opens; crash or stale takeover; interruption or power loss; parent-, database-, or project-root path identity; installers or file associations; or Windows, macOS, or ARM64. Third-party activation gating and legacy Soundscaper library migration remain deliberately outside this slice.

On a latest authoritative exact-schema-9 shared load, the renderer admits at most 4,094 reachable timeline, Project Bin, and fallback sources against the pre-existing latest recipient-local exact-schema-9 snapshot of the same project, which binds logical identity, kind, storage key, MIME type, and media geometry. Compatible same-kind descriptors sharing one physical storage key are verified once; a conflicting binding rejects. Declared payload geometry is capped at 65,536 PCM chunks, while one cumulative 64 GiB budget charges canonical audio archive bytes, including four framing bytes per chunk, and recipient-local video metadata sizes together. A successful body qualification reads selected metadata before and after that body, fully consumes ordered Float32Array PCM with exact chunk, channel, and frame geometry and matching supplied index or frame fields, and hashes each genuine Blob with SHA-256 through bounded 4 MiB windows. Legacy PCM-on-read migration and media-digest backfill are disabled. A pre-existing retained-video digest must match when present; audio and digestless retained video are availability- and geometry- or size-qualified but are not authenticated against a prior content digest. Every failure raised by this repository admission, including mismatch of that video digest, occurs before local shadow save or activation, while the later controller-owned rendered-fallback-declaration digest check follows repository shadowing. A source-free latest load performs zero source or media I/O. The bootstrap lifetime signal preserves exact cancellation during admission; one repository instance keeps latest load, save, and delete serialized per project; project publication and retention protect durable storage keys. A real-store mixed audio and video fixture qualifies bytes already present and bound by the latest local snapshot, while composed cross-product evidence covers source-free success and missing recipient PCM refusal that preserves the pre-existing revision and does not activate. This is a bounded sequential admission-time readability check, not an atomic snapshot, media transfer, publisher authentication, or a durable byte lease.

After metadata-journal recovery and before the host is exposed, main-only startup maintenance walks the authoritative project-file inventory by monotonic row IDs. It captures a cycle high-water and persists a cursor, scans at most 100,000 rows per invocation in at most 64-row batches, and surfaces scanned, protected, reclaimed, and complete state. Every destructive batch holds a SQLite immediate writer transaction, revalidates the exact live lease before and after filesystem work, and rebuilds portable case-folded reachability from the integrity-checked current catalog plus both previous and next snapshots of any pending prepared or committed journal. An unreachable registered canonical regular project file is synchronously renamed to a deterministic noncatalogable quarantine derived from its portable metadata path and unlinked while catalog writers are excluded; a crash-left quarantine is safely retried. Unregistered stage, canonical, forged quarantine, and foreign files do not consume inventory budget and remain untouched. A real 100,001-row fixture proves successive bounded passes reach the suffix, while later inserts wait for the next high-water cycle. Batches yield for lease renewal and cancellation. Static root symlinks fail closed; symlinked entries, malformed names, directories, and managed media remain untouched. Focused tests also cover prepared and committed recovery, update and delete cleanup, higher-token path reuse, corruption, portable case aliases, idempotence, and reclamation-failure lease release. The compiled runtime and desktop staging inventory include the collector without adding IPC.

The main project writer registers a unique random canonical stage path with its planned project row in one immediate SQLite transaction under the exact lease and fencing token before exclusive open. When exact-lease cleanup is acknowledged, an exclusive-open failure retires only the registration without unlinking the path, while an error after exclusive creation targets that registered random stage for removal. Lost-lease or failed cleanup leaves the registration for takeover. Materialization requires the exact metadata path, stage path, lease ID, and fencing token, then renames the file, syncs its containing directory, marks the project materialized, and removes the stage row in one before-and-after fenced transaction. Startup maintenance walks the separate monotonic stage inventory with a persisted high-water and cursor. A persisted project/stage schedule alternates at-most-64-row batches under the shared 100,000-row invocation cap. Current exact-lease stage rows remain live; prior-lease regular files are removed, missing rows retire, and non-regular targets or non-direct parents stay untouched and inventoried. Canonical rows with outstanding stages remain ineligible. Stage-cycle completion persists and consumes a rescan flag atomically with restarting the canonical high-water, so cleanup cannot leave an already-scanned parent behind. Unregistered and legacy pre-inventory stage-looking files remain foreign, do not consume the budget, and are untouched. Focused crash, takeover, low- and mixed-cap, rollback, acknowledged-collision, non-regular, and unregistered-file fixtures qualify this cooperative-writer lifecycle without adding renderer IPC.

residualRisks.exposure: Bounded sequential recipient-local admission now qualifies already-present bytes bound by the latest local snapshot for a latest exact schema 9 shared load and refuses bytes observed missing during admission, but source and media bytes remain in product-local shadows. This is not an atomic snapshot: selected metadata is reread around each body, but body reads are not transactionally bound to it; same-metadata replacement during sequential observations can go undetected, and replacement or deletion afterward is not fenced. Separate repository instances or processes are not serialized. Injected non-cooperative provider work may continue after rejection; audio and digestless retained video are not authenticated against prior content digests; and the prerequisite local descriptor binding is not publisher authentication. Managed-media copy, consolidation, relink, and managed storage are absent, so a fresh recipient has neither that descriptor snapshot nor a byte-acquisition outcome; codec playback is not cross-product qualified. Compatibility beyond retained V1-V8 raw-document migrations, especially migration from the prior shared v1 scope or product-private Soundscaper libraries, is deliberately deferred and unsupported, not a current required control; Audacity project import is a separate boundary.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Before claiming portable source-bearing handoff, establish an explicit recipient-local descriptor binding and fresh-recipient relink, copy, consolidation, or managed-storage acquisition outcome; hold or revalidate the selected byte identity through activation and playback with a durable snapshot, lease, or compare-and-swap binding; and qualify the packaged two-product source-bearing lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Packaged two-product source-bearing fixtures establish the recipient-local descriptor binding, acquire bytes through an explicit relink, copy, consolidation, or managed-storage outcome, and hold or revalidate a stable recipient byte identity through activation and playback, while retaining the tested missing-at-admission refusal.

residualRisks.exposure: The maintained dedicated Linux x64 source-free packaged preload/IPC/multi-process/executable lifecycle is qualified. The remaining OS and architecture matrix is not. Parent- or database-path replacement, parent-directory power-loss durability, Windows directory-sync and deny-delete behavior, and junction or time-of-check/time-of-use handling are not qualified on every supported OS and architecture. An interrupted reservation can therefore leave a foreign regular collision at its registered random stage path eligible for later stale-stage cleanup, while registered non-regular or symlink stage replacements remain untouched and inventoried rather than being adopted or deleted.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Extend packaged source-free cross-product qualification beyond Linux x64 and qualify interruption recovery with platform-specific path-identity and durability controls.
acceptanceCriteria: Packaged OS/architecture smoke and fault-injection tests cover process handoff, power loss at every publication and reclamation phase, parent-directory persistence, database and project-root identity, Windows sharing behavior, and junction handling.

risks.title: Current user-authored Nyquist source escapes its bounded WebAssembly worker envelope
risks.actor: A Nyquist program loops, requests excessive memory or output, or attempts file access.

currentControls.summary: Nyquist runs in a dedicated worker with validated protocol and source/input/output bounds, a 256-MiB WebAssembly memory ceiling, timeout and abort termination, and disabled C file-I/O stubs.

risks.title: Future third-party Web effect packages gain same-origin JavaScript authority
risks.actor: A future reviewed effect package is malicious, compromised, or has a confused-deputy import surface.

currentControls.summary: The maintained registry currently exposes only reviewed, source-pinned bundled Nyquist plug-ins; no generic package loader exists.

residualRisks.exposure: A reviewed Web effect package ABI, import allowlist, signature/hash policy, revocation model, and worker lifecycle are not implemented.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Instantiate pure WebAssembly packages in dedicated workers through a minimal allowlisted host ABI; do not import arbitrary third-party JavaScript into the application origin.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed ABI, forbidden import, timeout, oversized output, hash mismatch, and revocation tests pass before a package loader is exposed.

risks.title: Future native media and render helpers compromise the UI process or remain alive after cancellation
risks.actor: Malformed input, a compromised helper binary, or a protocol peer sends invalid messages or refuses shutdown.

currentControls.summary: The current versioned preload bridge exposes no native helper, process-spawn, or plug-in-host channel.

residualRisks.exposure: No bounded helper protocol, process supervisor, sandbox policy, crash quarantine, or binary attestation exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define a versioned bounded IPC protocol and supervised process lifecycle with least-privilege OS policy and verified binaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Crash, hang, malformed message, oversized payload, binary mismatch, and cancellation tests pass without exposing raw spawn authority to the renderer.

risks.title: Future native audio or video plug-ins execute with ambient user-account authority
risks.actor: A third-party VST3, CLAP, AU, LV2, or OFX binary is malicious, vulnerable, or incompatible.

currentControls.summary: The current renderer bridge and editor registry expose no native plug-in discovery, loading, or execution surface.

residualRisks.exposure: No plug-in discovery allowlist, quarantine, permissions, compatibility process, consent UX, or signing policy exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Treat native plug-ins as arbitrary code, isolate them in a supervised host, minimize filesystem and network authority, and disclose residual OS authority to the user.
acceptanceCriteria: Host compromise, crash recovery, denial, scanning, consent, revocation, and per-platform packaging tests pass before discovery is enabled.

risks.title: Cancelled or superseded jobs continue consuming resources or publish late results
risks.actor: A user cancels, switches projects, closes a renderer, or starts a replacement task while I/O is active.

currentControls.summary: Controller tasks receive AbortSignals and generation checks prevent stale results from replacing current UI state. Matching native-import ownership clears and republishes the global importing flag even after an external project generation change, while an older owner cannot clear newer work.

Native .scape open/save tasks pass their AbortSignal through archive, tested storage, and file publication boundaries; cancellation rolls staged assets and project revisions back before the task settles.

Public .scape inspection starts one distinct named controller task before archive work, snapshots caller options, and composes the caller signal with the owned signal. Replacement, project switching, and terminal disposal synchronously abort ownership; a post-await current-task check rejects signal-ignoring late results, and finally releases completed tasks. Inspection passes that signal into its project-collision read. The default store promptly races stalled database admission, aborts and drains an active read-only IndexedDB transaction, and preserves the exact cancellation reason. The service gives the defensive read-only Scape boundary a narrow retention capability; that boundary normalizes and registers an injected lookup with the same inspection admission in its synchronous read callback before returning the provider promise to the abort race, promptly rejects a signal-ignoring provider, closes its archive reader, and suppresses the late result or failure. Focused regressions also pin switch cancellation before awaited project work and verify composition-root routing.

Every public .scape inspection registers before its first await with a controller-level coordinator that retains current and superseded generations through archive-reader cleanup and registered injected collision-provider settlement. Admission reserves one of eight lower-only production slots synchronously before task creation or archive work. Project-switch admission installs a reference-counted temporary fence, cancels captured Scape tasks with one shared legacy supersession AbortError per admission, and rejects later admission; controller disposal installs a permanent fence with the exact lifetime reason. Cancellation, fencing, close, and drain arm one lower-only 30-second settlement deadline per inspection, reused without reset by overlapping barriers. Only rejection with the exact registration abort reason is benign; provider fulfillment or rejection releases retention without replacing that primary outcome. Deadline expiry is a typed non-benign barrier failure, aggregates with observed cleanup failures, and does not remove or release the inspection's capacity charge until retained work actually settles. Project switching rejects before project work on timeout, while disposal continues remaining engine and storage teardown before rejecting.

Public .scape file opens start one replaceable request task before inspection and carry its signal through one closed open decision and native-open settlement. The UI owns one opaque prompt and settles its exact identity only once. Replacement, project switching, and terminal disposal synchronously clear and reject pending prompts with exact cancellation reasons, while explicit user cancel resolves normally. Matching native-import cleanup republishes the cleared busy flag even when project activation changed the original generation; expected lifecycle unwind is suppressed from generic errors. Compatible collision prompts preserve their existing focus behavior, while incompatible prompts default to Cancel; the shared dialog shell provides focus containment, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration.

Within one project-store instance, every streamed-writer begin that passes synchronous argument and signal validation registers with the per-store lifecycle before its first awaited backend operation. After staging preparation returns, the admission attaches its chunk-token or OPFS-path identity and terminal writer abort before begin can return. Clear establishes a temporary admission fence and close a permanent one; both reject later begins, signal and drain captured pre-staging begins, abort staged chunk or OPFS sinks and active writers, and cannot settle while a pre-fence begin could still return a live writer or publish late state. A cleanup failure rejects the maintenance barrier instead of reporting successful quiescence.

Within one AudioEditorProjectStore, the facade tracks one active clear and one shared close barrier. Clear establishes media maintenance and captures its backend-admission promise before its first wait. Close installs the permanent media fence and terminal facade state before its first await, then joins an already admitted clear. Concurrent close callers return the same terminal-cleanup promise, and an admitted clear retains its normal memory fallback when database availability fails while an unrelated pending database admission remains fenced when no clear is active. The overlap regressions prove clear settles before close and neither close caller settles before the captured media operation drains.

IndexedDB schema v5 publishes generation-fenced ownership before streamed chunk or OPFS staging exists. Chunk writes and immutable metadata publication validate the live lease in their mutation transaction; clear rotates the generation atomically, cleanup retains live identities and reclaims expired staging, and degraded memory mode never creates uncoordinated shared OPFS staging.

Every retained-media load registers synchronously with the same per-store lifecycle coordinator used by streamed writers before its first await. Clear holds a temporary admission fence and close a permanent fence; both signal captured loads through cancellation linked with the caller and await terminal settlement before data deletion or database close. The multi-chunk regression proves a digest that observes the maintenance abort cannot publish version-one provenance or return a payload after maintenance settles; a standalone clear then reopens admission while close remains terminal.

IndexedDB schema v6 atomically removes spoofable provenance fields from pre-cutover media rows; markerless rows expose no inherited hash, acquire one retryable version-zero Web-Crypto content claim, hash stored bytes in bounded four-MiB reads, and publish version-one SHA-256 only through a token-checked compare-and-set that rejects stale delete or replacement races.

Project saves choose one target before asynchronous flush, stream through a plan-aware bounded destination, abort staging on project switch or failure, compare independent exact byte counts, and perform one explicit non-cancellable publication commit. Cancellation after a successful commit is reported as committed without stale success UI.

The maintained direct WAV, AIFF, BWF, and admitted BW64 PCM route selects its target before rendering, propagates the owned export task signal and realtime progress through destination preparation and rendering, and serially awaits at-most-four-MiB coalesced destination writes while a channel-aware 16,384-frame queue bounds pending planar Float32 PCM to 32 MiB. Exact desktop `audio-pcm-mix` sessions negotiate four-MiB chunks; generic and project sessions remain at one MiB. Failure or cancellation before commit aborts and awaits staging cleanup, preserving a primary failure together with a cleanup failure. Planned, encoder-finalized, and destination-written counts agree before one explicit non-cancellable commit. If ownership is lost during commit, the controller returns the committed result without stale success UI publication. A committed-result size disagreement is reported as a post-publication integrity failure, not as rollback. Nonqualifying export paths remain unchanged. Focused Node tests cover the full cancellation, cleanup-failure, ownership, and commit-boundary contract; the focused Node AIFF, BWF, and BW64 mid-stream cancellation cases each observe one abort, no close, and no commit. The opt-in 385 MiB witness cancels its second run after the first coalesced 4 MiB PCM destination write and observes one abort without close or commit and no partial publication. The ten Chromium and Firefox WAV, AIFF, BWF, and BW64 format/engine cases cancel after PCM bytes reach the injected target and observe one abort with no close, commit, or publication, proving the same pre-commit rollback. In the current-import pristine-passthrough BW64 witness, visible progress precedes the completed publication without Blob fallback, while the cancellation run aborts without publication. This does not qualify arbitrary third-party or legacy opaque-only BW64, edited projects, or whole-file identity. WebKit remains unqualified because its pinned runtime cannot launch on this host. Packaged Soundscaper Linux x64 acceptance is WAV only under Electron 43: cancellation independently observes a 33,554,476-byte staging file, inspects no more than 65,536 bytes to validate RIFF geometry and nonzero payload, then verifies the destination is absent and staging is removed. The completed run observes no browser download. The smoke bypasses the native picker after save-choice validation.
